en.name: Julius I
en.summary: A pope who defended the exiled Athanasius of Alexandria and asserted Rome's right to be consulted in major Eastern doctrinal disputes.
en.body: Julius I became a vigorous defender of orthodoxy during the Arian controversy, giving refuge in Rome to Athanasius of Alexandria after his exile and convening a synod that vindicated him. In a pointed letter to Eastern bishops who had proceeded without him, Julius asserted that matters concerning major sees should not be settled without Rome being consulted — an early and influential statement of papal prerogative that helped shape the Council of Sardica's later canons on appeals to Rome.
